short: The last samurai charge, met by conscripts with Gatling guns.
full:
By September 1877 the Satsuma Rebellion was finished. Saigo Takamori, a leading figure of the Meiji Restoration who had broken with the government over the dismantling of samurai privilege, had marched north in January and been stopped at Kumamoto Castle. Driven the length of Kyushu, he reached the hill of Shiroyama above Kagoshima with about 500 men left, many of them armed only with swords.

Government forces under Yamagata Aritomo, some 30,000 conscripts with artillery and Gatling guns, dug siege lines around the hill and bombarded it. The final assault came before dawn on 24 September. The remaining samurai charged once their ammunition ran out; Saigo was mortally wounded and died on the slope. The defeat settled the argument that had run through the Meiji reforms: a conscript army with modern firearms had replaced the warrior caste, which ceased to exist as a legal class. Saigo was posthumously pardoned in 1889. Sabaton's "Shiroyama", from The Last Stand (2016), is about the final assault.
